# pulse_user (Resource)

A dashboard user: a person who signs in to the Pulse dashboard.

A user created here has no password. They sign in with single sign-on (link their identity with `pulse_user_identity`, or let a `pulse_sso_provider` with just-in-time provisioning match them by email), or an administrator issues them a one-time password link from the dashboard's Users page.

`roles` holds only the roles assigned here; roles a user gets from SSO group mappings (`pulse_sso_mapping`) are reported in `sso_roles` and are never removed by this resource. Changing a user's roles or disabling them signs them out everywhere.

Pulse refuses to remove the administrator role from, disable or delete the last enabled administrator, and a token cannot disable or delete its own user.

Import with the user ID or the email address.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An operator who signs in with SSO. The user has no password; link their identity with
# pulse_user_identity, or issue a password link from the dashboard's Users page.
resource "pulse_user" "alice" {
  email        = "alice@example.com"
  display_name = "Alice"
  roles        = ["operator"]
}

# A read-only account, disabled for now.
resource "pulse_user" "contractor" {
  email        = "contractor@example.com"
  display_name = "Contractor"
  roles        = ["viewer"]
  mfa_required = true
  enabled      = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `display_name` (String) Name shown in the dashboard (at most 128 bytes).

### Optional

- `email` (String) Email address, in lower case (Pulse stores emails in lower case). Optional for users who sign in only with SSO. Pulse cannot change a user's email, so changing it forces a new resource.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the user can sign in. Default `true`. Disabling a user signs them out everywhere.
- `mfa_required` (Boolean) Require the user to enroll an authenticator app (TOTP) for password sign-in even when their roles do not demand it. Default `false`. Pulse also requires it for password accounts holding roles listed in its `PULSE_MFA_REQUIRED_ROLES` setting (`administrator` and `operator` by default); that requirement is not shown as a difference here.
- `roles` (Set of String) Roles assigned to the user directly: `administrator`, `operator`, `auditor`, `viewer`. Defaults to none (for example for a user who gets every role from SSO group mappings). Roles from SSO mappings are not listed here; see `sso_roles`.

### Read-Only

- `all_roles` (Set of String) Every role the user holds: `roles` together with `sso_roles`.
- `has_password` (Boolean) Whether the user has set a password.
- `id` (String) User ID.
- `mfa_enrolled` (Boolean) Whether the user has enrolled an authenticator app.
- `provisioned_via` (String) How the user was created: `admin` (by an administrator, including this provider), `jit` (just-in-time on their first SSO sign-in), or another way such as an invitation.
- `sso_roles` (Set of String) Roles the user holds through SSO group mappings, updated at each SSO sign-in.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By user ID
terraform import pulse_user.alice 01j9z6q7m3c8k2v5x4w1n0p9r8

# By email address
terraform import pulse_user.alice alice@example.com
```
